title: Final review: everything the UI consistency branch changes

steps.headline: This deck shows everything the UI consistency branch changes, so you can decide whether to merge it.
steps.changed: WHAT IT IS: three weeks of work making every screen follow one design guide — 260 app changes (690 files), over 230 workspace changes (the guide, decks, tools), 4 game-server changes. EVERY SCREEN: all 368 practice screens were photographed on master and on the branch; all 241 that exist on both changed, 127 are new screens or states, 6 are gone (removed features). WHAT IS GREEN (checked today): the full desktop check (types, every test, dead code, lint, design lint, rules, every screen opens, the saved click paths); Android 1,839 tests, 0 failures; game server 389 tests, 5 runs in a row, after fixing two tests that failed only when the machine was busy; documentation links 572 of 572.
steps.notice: DEPLOY ORDER: when you merge, the game server goes live first and must be live BEFORE any app with incognito reaches people — an older server would show an incognito player as online. HOW TO USE: each section opens with a words slide; pictures read Yes keep it / No revert it; slides marked 'Approved' you already said yes to; slides marked 'Not reviewed before' are new to you. Questions only you can answer are near the end, then a list of everything NOT done.

steps.headline: Master is the app today; Branch is after this work. Pictures come in your theme and one light theme.
steps.changed: Each picture slide shows the same screen on master (labelled Master) and on the branch (Branch). The swatches at the top switch between Halftone Dimension (your theme) and Meadow Mist (a light theme). A slide with several screens lays them side by side. A slide with only a Branch picture is a state the practice app could not show before (a new screen, or a moment like a failure) — it reads Yes keep it / No remove it.
steps.notice: Pictures come from the practice app with made-up data, so names, files and friends are samples. One thing that looks new but is not: Marketplace's 'Connect your stuff' row appears only because the practice app gained sample connections — the row itself is unchanged.

steps.path: A decision only you can make
steps.headline: When an incognito player is claimed to have left a game, keep privacy first?
steps.today: In a two-player game, if your opponent leaves and doesn't return, your app can claim a forfeit win; the server checks the opponent is really gone.
steps.problem: An incognito player counts as 'gone' for that check. A normal app only claims after the opponent's game drops, but a modified app could claim a forfeit against an incognito player still playing, and win wrongly. Counting them as present instead (tried as F28) would tell the claimer the incognito player is online.
steps.proposal: Keep privacy first: incognito stays invisible, at the cost of a possible wrong loss against a cheater.
